title: The Animal Whose Blood Can Neutralize Snake Venom

scenes.text: Rattlesnakes bite this animal. It shrugs.
It's the Virginia opossum. Scientists have known since the 1940s that it resists venom.
Researchers found a peptide in its blood that neutralizes the poison.
In lab tests, mice given venom plus the peptide showed no signs of illness.
It worked against western diamondback rattlesnake venom and Russell's viper venom.
Someday, a new antivenom could come from the humble opossum.
